title: Dance of Virtuous Maidens and Valiant Youths (Ki Shad Ki Rang Bad Thei-Sotti)
khasi_title: Ki Shad Ki Rang Bad Thei-Sotti
cultural_context: Vivid lyric describing the circular ceremonial choreography where maidens glide with downcast modest eyes inside while warriors dance guard on the outer perimeter, from 'Ki Sur Ba Dang Sawa'.

khasi: Ki shad ki rang bad ki thei-sotti,
Ha khet ba kyntang ka Weiking;
Ki thei-sotti ki peit sha madan,
Da ka akor ba donburom bad ba jar-jar;
Ki rangbah ki shad sawdong jong ki,
Kum ki nongiada ba ieng skhem;
Ki symphiah rupa ki kynshoit suiñ,
Ha ka sngi ba phyrnai ka pyrem.
english: The youths and virtuous maidens dance,
Upon the sacred ground of Weiking;
The virtuous maidens look modestly downward,
With quiet grace and noble etiquette;
The brave youths dance encircling them,
Their silver yak-tail whisks sweep through the air,
Beneath the radiant sunshine of springtime.

khasi: Ka paila mukmor ka kyrsoi jingshai,
Ki kynjri ksiar ki sawa jai-jai;
Hapdeng ka ksing ba kiew bad hiar,
Ka dohnud ka dap da ka kmen;
Dei kane ka shad ba buh ki kpa,
Ban pynpaw ka hok bad ka jingsotti
Ha khmat u Blei Nongbuh Nongthaw.
english: The coral-bead necklaces gleam with light,
The golden filigree chains whisper rhythmically;
Amidst the rising and falling beats of the drum,
The heart overflows with pure joy;
This is the sacred dance ordained by the ancestors,
Before God, the Supreme Creator and Architect.

vocabulary.symphiah: ceremonial silver whisks held by dancing warriors
vocabulary.weiking: historic sacred dancing grounds in Shillong
vocabulary.nongbuh nongthaw: the Supreme Creator who ordains all things
